newsitem.title: USA: Dow Industrials steady at midday, advance tough.
newsitem.headline: Dow Industrials steady at midday, advance tough.

text.p: The Dow Industrials were steady at midday but a bond market rally failed to overcome investors' concern ahead of next week's U.S. Presidential election or the stock market's own exhaustion.
"You have a situation in which the buyers are stepping away from the plate ahead of the election," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
The Dow was up three at 5975 while advancing issues inched ahead of declining ones on volume of about 212 million shares.

"Buyers are planning to keep their powder dry until they see what happens to the market on election day (November 5)," Bleier said. "A victory by President Clinton has been discounted. But will Congress become Democrat? Maybe. What does that mean for the market?"
In addition to trepidation ahead of the election, not to mention a full week of data climaxing with Friday's October jobs report, the market has become overbought.
"Between July and mid-October, the S&P 500 was up 15 percent from its intraday lows," said Chris Callies, chief investment strategist at CS First Boston.

"The market is due for a pullback and there is ample psychological justification -- the employment data is due this week, the (third quarter real) GDP and the all-important election," Callies said. "It's no wonder that investors don't want to stick their necks out."

U.S. Treasuries were strong, with the long bond up 1-18/32 to yield 6.71 percent. The rally was sparked by a weaker than forecast 0.6 percent increase in the third quarter employee cost index, compared with a 0.8 increase the previous quarter.
Bonds extended their gains after the October index of U.S. consumer confidence came in weaker than had been expected.
The index fell to 106.2 in October from a revised 111.8 in September. An October reading of 110.6 had been expected, according to a Reuter survey of U.S. economists.
As the afternoon progressed, the Industrials finally felt the heat of the bond market and began to climb higher. The Dow was up 23 points at 5996.
High techs remained under pressure, however, with the tech-laden Nasdaq Composite Index down seven points at 1209.
"The Nasdaq is looking rather bleak in the near term," Bleier said.
Salomon Brothers analyst David Childe said that the stock of CompUSA Inc could come under pressure due to worsening conditions in the computer retail industry.
"There has been a distinct softening in overall retail computer sales over the past few weeks," Childe said in a research note.

CompUSA was down 4-3/4 at 52-5/8. International Business Machines Corp was down 7/8 at 126-1/4, Compaq Computer Corp was down 2-3/8 at 68-1/4, Hewlett-Packard Co was down 7/8 at 44-3/8 and Tandy Corp was down 3/4 at 39-1/4.
